summary.headline: The Conservation Commission reviewed a turf field conversion at Fay School and renewed its environmental consulting contract.
summary.summary: The Southborough Conservation Commission reviewed a notice of intent for athletic field renovations and artificial turf installation at the Fay School complex, continuing the hearing pending peer review and state DEP numbers. The commission also renewed its peer review and consulting contract with Lucas Environmental with terms addressing conflict-of-interest vetting for smaller local jobs. In addition, members issued several certificates of compliance, tabled a compliance request for an auto facility on Turnpike Road due to site violations, and affirmed that golf course irrigation upgrades align with open space restrictions.

topics.title: Fay School athletic fields redevelopment at 0 Marlboro Junction
topics.summary: Field Engineering presented a notice of intent on behalf of the New England Football Club and Fay School to reconstruct existing athletic fields at 0 Marlboro Junction. The project involves converting two grass soccer fields to artificial turf, relocating a natural turf baseball field, and adding parking on the Marlborough side of the property, with work extending into the 100-foot wetland buffer and riverfront areas. Commission members discussed the history of previous riverfront alterations on the site and confirmed that the planned crumb-rubber turf system will be tested to verify it is PFAS-free.
key_details: Address: 0 Marlboro Junction (Map 91, Lot 6) on the Southborough-Marlborough line
Includes converting two natural grass soccer fields to artificial turf and shifting them southward
Baseball field will be relocated within the riverfront area but kept as natural grass
Sprinturf crumb-rubber turf system with a nine-inch stone infiltration bed and underdrains
One commissioner recused due to employment with Fay School
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to September 17, 2024, pending state DEP file number and peer review.
topics.why_it_matters: The proposal involves significant construction near protected riverfront and wetland zones and installs artificial turf over a large athletic complex shared across town borders.

topics.title: 250 Turnpike Road townhome development continuance
topics.summary: The commission opened a continued public hearing for a notice of intent to construct 32 rental townhomes at 250 Turnpike Road and 0 Parkerville Road. The applicant requested a continuance because peer review funds were recently received and the technical review is just getting underway.
key_details: Address: 250 Turnpike Road and 0 Parkerville Road (Map 27, Lots 46 and 2A)
Proposal entails 32 rental townhomes
Peer review has just started

topics.title: 0 Southville Road apartment buildings continuance
topics.summary: The commission opened a continued public hearing on a notice of intent and stormwater management permit application for two apartment buildings and related sitework at 0 Southville Road. The applicant requested a continuance to revise plans in response to peer review feedback.
key_details: Address: 0 Southville Road (Map 5, Lot 8)
Applicant: Apartments at Southville Road LLC
Scope includes two apartment buildings and site infrastructure

topics.title: Lucas Environmental consulting contract renewal
topics.summary: The commission reviewed an agreement renewal with its long-term environmental consultant, Lucas Environmental, whose previous contract expired on June 30. Members discussed rate adjustments, municipal budget pressures, and the potential for the consultant to work on smaller private residential applications in Southborough provided projects are vetted with the conservation agent to prevent conflicts of interest.
key_details: Contract renewal covers a two-year period through June 30, 2026
Includes a flat rate increase of $10 per hour across positions
Lucas Environmental agreed to bill work done in July and August at previous fiscal year rates
Consultant may take small private homeowner projects only after conflict review with the town agent

topics.title: Certificate of compliance for Route 9 Sarsenstone subdivision
topics.summary: The commission considered a certificate of compliance for DEP File 290-100 on Route 9 and Sarsenstone Way. The conservation agent located historic Department of Public Works as-built road profiles and detention basin drawings confirming that the 1991 subdivision requirements were met.
key_details: DEP File number 290-100
Original permit dates back to a 1991 subdivision approval
As-built plans on file at DPW confirm drainage and road conditions
topics.outcome: Full certificate of compliance approved unanimously 5-0.

topics.title: Administrative amendment for 45 Southville Road deck replacement
topics.summary: The conservation agent presented an administrative amendment under an open septic repair order at 45 Southville Road. The homeowner requested permission to replace an aging rear deck and front stairs in-kind using hand-dug footings without expanding the building footprint.
key_details: DEP File number 290-1133 at 45 Southville Road
Replaces an existing deteriorated rear deck and front stairs
Work involves hand-dug footings and no expansion of footprint

topics.title: Certificate of compliance for 38 Sears Road pool renovation
topics.summary: The conservation agent reported on an inspection at 38 Sears Road for completed swimming pool liner and patio renovations, which included the addition of a pergola on existing hardscape. The surrounding lawn has been stabilized with sod and all construction debris was cleared.
key_details: DEP File number 290-1132 at 38 Sears Road
Work included pool liner replacement, patio work, and a pergola within existing hardscape
Lawn stabilized and no encroachment beyond the work limit
topics.outcome: Full certificate of compliance approved unanimously 5-0.

topics.title: Partial certificate of compliance for 2 Watkins Lane
topics.summary: The commission reviewed an outstanding title complication involving multiple merged orders of conditions for a common driveway development on Watkins Lane. The conservation agent recommended issuing a partial certificate of compliance for 2 Watkins Lane after reviewing historical aerial photos confirming that lawn mowing and site disturbance stayed within the originally approved limits.
key_details: Affects DEP File numbers 290-581, 290-586, 290-587, and 290-588
Four permits had previously been consolidated into one shared order
Releases 2 Watkins Lane from the encumbrance
topics.outcome: Partial certificate of compliance approved unanimously 5-0.

topics.title: Certificate of compliance review for 355 Turnpike Road commercial site
topics.summary: The conservation agent reported on a compliance inspection at 355 Turnpike Road, an automotive repair and fence business site where a septic replacement was permitted. The inspection uncovered expanded unapproved asphalt paving, uncleaned catch basins with oil sheen, and an uncleared stormwater outlet, preventing release of the order of conditions.
key_details: DEP File number 290-1099 at 355 Turnpike Road
Applicant seeks certificate of compliance to obtain a Class 2 used car dealer license
Site inspection found unpermitted pavement expansion and unmaintained catch basins
Stormwater outlet at the rear of the property remains uncleaned
topics.outcome: Request tabled pending required site cleanup, basin maintenance, and engineering clarification.

topics.title: Southborough Golf Course irrigation project update
topics.summary: The conservation agent and commission members discussed preliminary plans for the Southborough Golf Course irrigation upgrade funded through the Community Preservation Committee. Both the conservation agent and Sudbury Valley Trustees confirmed that the proposed small pump station near Cordaville Road constitutes allowable incidental infrastructure under the property conservation restriction, and utility lines will be directionally bored beneath the stream rather than open-trenched.
key_details: Irrigation upgrade funded in part through Community Preservation Act funds
Sudbury Valley Trustees and conservation agent confirmed a pump station is permitted under the conservation restriction
Pump station structure will resemble a low-profile utility cabinet near Cordaville Road
Water lines will be directionally bored under the stream corridor to avoid surface disruption
topics.outcome: Commission reached consensus supporting the design approach ahead of formal filings.

topics.title: Conservation Agent updates: Knotweed, Breakneck Hill dump, and Costco filing
topics.summary: The conservation agent shared administrative updates on several town projects. Property managers at 120 Turnpike Road submitted a late-summer foliar spray treatment plan for invasive Japanese knotweed around a pond. The town plans to rescind more than $700,000 in unissued borrowing authority for the Breakneck Hill Road dump at the upcoming Town Meeting while preserving $176,000 for final capping restoration. Additionally, Costco submitted an expanded Environmental Notification Form for its proposal at 21 Computer Drive.
key_details: 120 Turnpike Road: Targeted backpack foliar herbicide application planned for Japanese knotweed
Breakneck Hill Dump: Town Meeting will vote to rescind over $700,000 in unused borrowing while retaining roughly $176,000 for site restoration
Costco: Expanded Environmental Notification Form filed for 21 Computer Drive
topics.outcome: Information presented with no formal action required.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The commission addressed routine procedural business, voting to approve the draft meeting minutes from July 29, 2024, after postponing the vote earlier in the meeting to establish a quorum of attendees from that date.
key_details: Minutes of July 29, 2024, approved as drafted
Vote passed 3-0 with two abstentions
